# **Stavvros**

Team Members: Sai Karthik Kata, AbdulMuqeet Mohammed, Antony G. Chackieth

# **What we're building**

Stavvros is a shared memory for the AI assistants that help software teams write code. It knows how all of a company's software fits together and why it was built that way, so the AI stops guessing.

Think of the guide a new engineer gets on their first day. Stavvros is that guide, written for AI, and it updates itself every time the software changes.

At its core, Stavvros solves the documentation problem from both ends. It makes old documentation easy to find, and it makes new code and documentation faster to write.

## **The problem**

AI assistants can now write much of a company's code, but they only see the small piece they're working on. Everything else is invisible to them: the other teams' systems, the planning documents, and the reasons behind past decisions.

**An example.** A developer at an online store asks an AI assistant to add a "refund" button. The assistant can see the checkout code. It can't see the payment system, which another team owns, or last year's planning document that explains the refund rules. So it guesses. The code looks right, passes a quick review, and breaks when real customers ask for refunds.

Even when the planning documents exist, they often fall out of date. An assistant that reads an old document confidently builds for a system that no longer exists.

## **Why now**

Developers increasingly let AI write the whole change and only check the finished result. That means the AI's knowledge now decides the quality of the software. A gap that once cost a developer an afternoon of digging now slips straight into the product.

## **Evidence**

We've seen this problem firsthand, and companies are already trying to solve it themselves.

* **Internships.** Our team members saw this at their internships, along with teams building their own in-house tools to work around it.  
* **Interviews.** Our customer interviews found other teams attempting their own fixes alongside existing tools. AI helps with coding, research, and documentation, but unclear scope and constant review limit time savings. Sharing, finding, and converting documents adds friction, highlighting the need for clearer specifications and easier collaboration.

Templates from FleetHD: This is the PRD template that they are currently implementing. Complaints from this interviewee:

* Word documents are hard to share, locate, and track.   
* Documentation is often overcomplicated yet unclear on scope, success criteria, and technical changes, causing agents to wander.

## **How it works**

A team connects Stavvros once, and from then on its AI assistants can ask it how the company's software works.

1. **Connect.** The team links Stavvros to where its code lives (GitHub for the MVP). We bring in the code, its change history, planning documents, and system diagrams.  
2. **Organize.** We connect related pieces, so a feature links to the team that owns it, the document that planned it, and the changes made to it.  
3. **Stay current.** Every change to the software updates the guide. If a document no longer matches the code, we flag it instead of passing along wrong information.  
4. **Answer.** In the refund example, the AI assistant asks Stavvros how payments work and gets the right rules before writing any code. Developers can look up the same answers themselves.

This also covers our mentor's point about documentation: keeping documents accurate for people is the same problem as keeping them accurate for AI.

**How Stavvros works**

## **Technical architecture**

Every push to GitHub flows through an ingestion pipeline into one knowledge base, which agents query over MCP.

![Technical architecture · sources to agents][image3]

Technical Architecture

* **Ingestion.** A GitHub Action fires on every push and sends code, commits, and docs to the pipeline. It extracts APIs and service boundaries, and chunks design docs and diagrams for indexing.  
* **Knowledge base.** A hybrid search index (keyword plus vector embeddings) sits beside a knowledge graph that links each API to its owning service, design doc, and commits. A drift detector compares docs against current code and flags mismatches. Developers can edit the graph directly, so a correction takes minutes instead of a conversation.  
* **Serving.** The query API is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, so Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can call it as a tool. The developer web app uses the same API.

**Measuring quality.** Our main benchmark is prompts saved, because it translates directly into the time and money a customer saves. Behind the scenes, we also use standard retrieval-quality metrics to check that Stavvros finds the right information for each question.

## **How we're different**

Other tools help AI read code. Stavvros also gives it the planning documents and diagrams that explain the code, and keeps them accurate.

| Type of tool | Examples | What it does | What it misses |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AI coding assistants | Claude Code, Codex | Reads the project it's working in | Other teams' systems and planning documents |
| Code search tools | Sourcegraph, Augment Code, Greptile | Searches code across many projects | Mostly code only; documents are an afterthought |
| Spec-writing tools | OpenSpec | Writes plans for one project at a time | Plans go out of date as code changes |
| Stavvros | — | Code, documents, and diagrams in one guide that stays current | Still to be proven |

## **Who it's for**

Our first customers are software companies with many teams, where no single person understands the whole system. Small teams benefit too, mainly through speed. When something changes, a developer can update the guide directly in minutes, instead of a teammate stopping their work to explain it. Fewer interruptions means faster development.

## **MVP**

Our first version should prove that an AI assistant does better work with Stavvros than without it.

1. **Connect to GitHub** and bring in a few related projects, starting with public, open-source ones.  
2. **Build the guide** for those projects, including their documents.  
3. **Let AI assistants ask it questions** while they write code.  
4. **Test it.** Our benchmark is prompts saved: how many fewer prompts a developer needs to finish the same task with Stavvros than without it. Customers can turn that number straight into money: fewer prompts means less developer time and lower AI usage costs.
